tip: Обе (obe = both) is the feminine form, matching сестры (syostry = sisters). Masculine or mixed groups take оба (oba).
Age uses the dative: Ей (yej = to her), not она (ona = she). Ей пятьдесят пять лет (yej pyatdesyat pyat let) means she is fifty-five.
Семеро (semero = seven) is a collective numeral for a group of people, an everyday alternative to plain семь (sem).
Две (dve = two) is the feminine form because капли (kapli = drops) is feminine. Masculine and neuter nouns take два (dva).
Work takes на (na), not в (v): на работе (na rabote = at work). Russian uses на for some locations where English says at or in.
Построен (postroyen = built) is a short passive participle and agrees with мост (most = bridge): masculine singular, so no ending.
For location, На (na = on) takes the prepositional case: втором этаже (vtorom etazhe = second floor), not the base form этаж (etazh).
With a fraction like Треть (tret = a third), the verb stays singular: опоздала (opozdala = was late), never plural.
Numbers from five up take the genitive plural: пятьсот (pyatsot = five hundred) рублей (rubley = of rubles), not рубли (rubli).
Numbers two, three, four take the genitive singular, not plural: четыре кусочка (chetyre kusochka = four pieces), not кусочки (kusochki).
Один из (odin iz = one of) is followed by the genitive plural: студентов (studentov = of students).
A reflexive passive uses -ся (sya): соблюдаются (soblyudayutsya = are followed). The doer takes the instrumental: сотрудниками (sotrudnikami = by staff).
Известно (izvestno = it is known) is an impersonal neuter form with no subject, followed by что (chto = that) and a clause.
В честь (v chest = in honor of) takes the genitive: поэта (poeta = of the poet). It is how Russian says named after someone.
Case, not position, marks roles, so the object can come first: Письма (pisma = letters) is the object, почтальон (pochtalyon = postman) the subject.
